title: SecureAFL: Secure Asynchronous Federated Learning

C-a.quote: By seamlessly detecting anomalous updates, reconstructing missing client contributions, and employing a resilient aggregation strategy, SecureAFL safeguards the learning process from malicious disruptions. This cohesive approach ensures that unreliable updates are excluded, plausible estimates compensate for incomplete participation, and the final aggregation remains robust, ultimately maintaining the integrity of the global model.
C-a.locator: §4.1 Overview; THE DISTRIBUTIVE TEST DECIDES THIS ROW'S COUNT AND IT IS THE TEST'S SECOND APPLICATION IN THE FRAME. The quoted passage is a joint attribution followed, in the very next sentence, by its own distribution across the three stages, and under the test articulated at row 47 (FedEMA-Distill) the distribution governs: detection -> "unreliable updates are excluded", aggregation -> "the final aggregation remains robust", estimation -> "plausible estimates compensate for incomplete participation". So the count reaches two on the paper's own words and the estimation stage is EXCISED. (1) FILTERING, purpose quoted at §4.2: "By enforcing this constraint, our method effectively filters out abrupt or suspicious changes in model updates, which may indicate malicious behavior, such as data poisoning or model manipulation.", with the motivation at the same section, "The motivation behind this approach is to identify anomalous or potentially malicious updates by comparing the smoothness of the current update against the historical distribution of client behaviors.". (2) BYZANTINE-ROBUST AGGREGATION (coordinate-wise median), purpose quoted at §4.1: "Finally, the server combines both received and estimated updates using a Byzantine-robust aggregation mechanism that limits the influence of malicious manipulations.". (3) L-BFGS UPDATE ESTIMATION IS EXCLUDED UNDER AMENDMENT 3: its stated purpose for inclusion is asynchrony and partial participation, not resisting poisoned updates -- "the missing updates by leveraging past model evolution, ensuring that the aggregation process remains balanced." (§4.1) and "Moreover, the update estimation mechanism allows SecureAFL to maintain a balanced aggregation process even when only a subset of clients actively contributes at each round, a scenario that becomes increasingly common in large-scale asynchronous systems." Abstract statement of the composition: "SecureAFL improves the robustness of asynchronous FL by detecting and discarding anomalous updates while estimating the contributions of missing clients. Additionally, it utilizes Byzantine-robust aggregation techniques, such as coordinate-wise median, to integrate the received and estimated updates."

C-b.quote: Moreover, the complementary design of SecureAFL ensures that even if some malicious updates bypass the filter at higher 𝛼 values, their influence is further mitigated by the update estimation process and coordinate-wise median aggregation.
C-b.locator: §6; RESIDUAL-COVERAGE KIND, the RKD kind, and stated as a property of the design rather than as a bare fact of assembly: the residue is named (malicious updates that bypass the filter at relaxed thresholds) and the stages that absorb it are named. The setting-level reason for needing a composed design at all is at §2: "However, this single-update and delayedupdate setting prevents the direct application of batch-based robust aggregation rules, requiring fundamentally different defense designs", i.e. one update per round makes batch robust aggregation inapplicable, which is why the estimation stage exists and why the median has anything to aggregate over. C-e.quote: This stability suggests that the Lipschitz-filtering mechanism effectively captures the normal smoothness patterns of benign client updates, even when the threshold is moderately relaxed or tightened.
C-e.locator: §6; the claim names one constituent and says what it contributes to the combined result. The variant-table version is "The results emphasize the critical role of filtering malicious updates, incorporating estimated updates, and utilizing a robust aggregation strategy like Median.", which attributes the composed outcome to each of the three stages by name. A third, about the aggregation rule, is at §6: "This stability can be attributed to SecureAFL ’s design, which aggregates both received and estimated updates using a Byzantinerobust rule, ensuring that the influence of malicious clients does not grow disproportionately with the number of participants.". A fourth, framework-level and about what the filter does NOT need, is "This robustness stems from the fact that SecureAFL does not depend on any auxiliary trusted dataset or global reference update; instead, it leverages historical client update trajectories and Lipschitz-based smoothness constraints that naturally adapt to heterogeneous data distributions."

coder_note:
DESIGN = YES, PRIMARY = NO, AND THE C-d IS THE CLEANEST COMPONENT CONTRAST THE FRAME HAS SEEN. Variant III is the RKD "without Clustering" arm with none of RKD's ambiguity: it does not delete a stage from the pipeline, it disables the FILTER'S DECISION while leaving the estimation stage and the Eq. (5) median in place and unmodified, so the composed system still has the same downstream mechanism, the same attacks, the same datasets and the same metrics, and the only thing that differs is the set of updates that reaches the median. That is the DROP counterfactual stated in the affirmative -- what DROP would have had to run and did not. A5 should use the Variant I / Variant III pair as the frame's canonical illustration that a single four-arm table can contain both the declined direction and the identifying one: Variant I swaps the DOWNSTREAM aggregation rule (FedAvg for median) and Variant III varies the UPSTREAM input to a fixed downstream, and the paper presents them as members of one list, exactly as FedSAC presented its two arms as "ablation experiments" in one breath.

THE DISTRIBUTIVE TEST GETS ITS SECOND APPLICATION AND ITS FIRST CONFIRMATION ON A DIFFERENT PAPER, WHICH MATTERS BECAUSE IT WAS ARTICULATED MID-CODING. At row 47 (FedEMA-Distill) I introduced the rule that when a paper attributes a conjunction of benefits to a conjunction of components, a sentence that DISTRIBUTES them governs over the joint sentence. A rule invented on one paper is a rule fitted to one paper. Here it applies unprompted and in the same direction: §4.1's joint sentence credits "detecting anomalous updates, reconstructing missing client contributions, and employing a resilient aggregation strategy" with safeguarding the model from malicious disruptions, and the NEXT sentence distributes -- exclusion to the filter, robustness to the aggregation, and to the estimation stage only "plausible estimates compensate for incomplete participation". Without the test I would have had to reach for rule 3 (take the reading that does not make the paper outcome-gated), which would have given the same C-a but for a worse reason. The test is now a two-paper rule with a consistent direction, and A5 reports it as such rather than as a one-off.

SIXTH INSTANCE OF AMENDMENT 3'S EXCISED-CONSTITUENT PATTERN, AND THE PURPOSE IS A NEW ONE. The excised purposes across the frame are now fairness/inclusion (2601.04930 PPFA-BA), encryption (2601.06466 SecureDyn-FL), secure aggregation (2602.22269 CQSA), temporal stability plus communication plus heterogeneity (2603.04422 FedEMA-Distill), privacy-sensitivity clipping plus variance reduction (2603.23472 Byz-Clip21-SGD2M), and now ASYNCHRONY AND PARTIAL PARTICIPATION (this row). That is six papers and at least eight distinct non-defense purposes, none of them privacy in more than two cases. The generalization CQSA's note originally reached -- that the excised constituent is "always the privacy one" -- is now wrong by a wide margin, and A5 must carry the corrected version: Amendment 3 excises whatever constituent the paper itself gives a non-defense purpose, and the distribution of those purposes is broad.

THE ALPHA SWEEP IS A SIXTH EXTERNAL TREATMENT OF COMPOSITION INVARIANCE AND ONLY THE SECOND THAT MEASURES IT. A3/A4 have been assembling the set: Fed-DPRoC PROVES a guarantee survives an upstream transform, SRFed's Thm 6.2 PROVES decisions unchanged, CQSA PROVES geometric preservation and then declines to measure, Byz-Clip21-SGD2M PROVES the opposite sign (a multiplicative penalty for enforcing privacy and Byzantine robustness together), and DDFed MEASURES no effect of upstream DP noise on downstream detection. SecureAFL is the second measurement, and for our purposes it is the better of the two: DDFed varies a PRIVACY knob, whereas SecureAFL varies the upstream DEFENSE'S OWN OPERATING POINT and then attributes the preserved outcome to the fixed downstream stages in so many words -- "Conversely, higher 𝛼 values admit more updates, improving learning efficiency while still maintaining strong robustness due to the subsequent estimation and Byzantine-robust aggregation steps." -- concluding "Importantly, the results indicate that SecureAFL is not overly sensitive to the precise tuning of 𝛼." and "Overall, these findings show that SecureAFL is robust to the choice of 𝛼 and can be reliably deployed without requiring fine-grained parameter tuning, which is particularly advantageous in practical FL systems where attack characteristics are unknown in advance.". So the honest external statement is now: six treatments, four analytic and two empirical, with one of the four analytic ones finding an ADVERSE interaction. That distribution, not a prevalence rate, is the strongest form of A3's claim, and A4 must not imply nobody measures the interaction.

WHAT KEEPS THIS ROW OUT OF THE PRIMARY IS ONLY C-d, AND EVERY OTHER CODE IS UNAMBIGUOUS. C-a rests on two purpose quotations, C-b on a residual-coverage reason with the residue named, C-c on the composed system's TER and ASR across four datasets and ten attacks, C-e on four separate constituent-level attributions. If C-d were NO this would be the frame's strongest primary. It is not, and the row is therefore evidence AGAINST the paper's implicit prevalence claim rather than for it -- which is the point of pre-registering the rubric before reading.

C-b's SECOND REASON IS OF THE INADMISSIBLE KIND AND IS RECORDED SO THE TAXONOMY STAYS HONEST. §2 explains that asynchronous FL delivers ONE update per round, which "prevents the direct application of batch-based robust aggregation rules". That is why the estimation stage exists: it manufactures the n-1 vectors the coordinate-wise median needs in order to have a population to take a median of. It is a real and good reason, and it is a reason of MATHEMATICAL CONVENIENCE -- the fifth kind, which C-b's frozen text does not admit -- so it does not carry the code. The residual-coverage sentence does. A5 should note that this is the second row (after FedSAC) where a mathematical-convenience reason was present and declined, and that in FedSAC's case declining it decided C-b = NO whereas here an admissible reason was independently present.

DOMAIN NOTE: first ASYNCHRONOUS FL paper in the frame, and its inclusion is correct under the frozen screen. Its value to the audit is structural: because the asynchronous single-update setting forces a three-stage pipeline where a synchronous paper would need only one aggregation rule, the paper cannot avoid composing, and it therefore had to think about what each stage receives. That is plausibly WHY the identifying contrast appears here and not in DROP.
